tldr: Add a single yes-or-no laughter question to the post-launch survey on every piece of brand video you make, then split every other answer by it.  OnePulse published the cleanest version of this all season on the Morrisons advert: 94 percent of the people who laughed rated it positively against 46 percent of those who did not.

Open your advert accounts today and switch off every setting that can alter creative after upload, then name one person who owns that panel.  A Japanese pizza chain published unapproved anime artwork last week because one of those settings had been left enabled, and viewers raised it before the brand did.

Count how many distinct things a viewer could want in your next seasonal film, and if the answer is one, add two more from ranges you already sell.  M&S put four ranges into one advert and posted 58 percent on the till question while the rest of the field sat between 32 and 42.

Demand peak, average concurrent and airtime together on every livestream sponsorship, and divide hours watched by airtime yourself when a seller has not given you the average.  IEM Beijing beat PGL Masters Bucharest on peak and delivered 38 percent less watch time, on a schedule nearly 20 hours shorter.

Write a co-streaming permission into your next live project before launch and name the creators you want using the feed.  The most-watched streamer on Twitch in October was one man narrating a tournament he does not own, at 22.2 million hours watched for the month, while no other creator passed 10 million hours.

Put the disclosure wording and placement you expect into the creator brief itself, and tell the creator in writing that nobody at your company may ask them to soften it.  Eighteen percent of creators surveyed say a brand asked them not to disclose a paid relationship in the last year, and the exposure reaches the advertiser.

Sort your footage into claim and mood before you commission anything generated, and permit generation only in the mood column.  Mark Rober's team keeps AI on scripts and thumbnails and away from the camera, because on a demonstration channel the unbroken shot is the receipt.

**THE FEED** · Monday 9 November 2026

**MORRISONS MADE THE FUNNIEST SUPERMARKET CHRISTMAS ADVERT SO FAR THIS SEASON, 94 PERCENT OF THE PEOPLE WHO LAUGHED AT IT RATED IT POSITIVELY AGAINST 46 PERCENT OF THE PEOPLE WHO DID NOT, AND MORRISONS HAS BOUGHT AN ADVERT BREAK INSIDE THE ONE TELEVISION PROGRAMME THAT IS NOTHING BUT PEOPLE REACTING TO TELEVISION**
The film went online yesterday morning and OnePulse rated it inside half an hour, which is how there is already a number on it.  The number is not the score.  The score is fine, 3.7 out of 5, fourth of the seven rated so far.  The number that matters is the split inside the sample: laugh at this advert and you are twice as likely to rate it well.  Then look at what Morrisons has booked for 20 November.

**1.** Add a single yes-or-no laughter question to the post-launch survey on every piece of brand video you make, then split every other answer by it.  OnePulse published the cleanest version of this all season on the Morrisons advert: 94 percent of the people who laughed rated it positively against 46 percent of those who did not.
**2.** Open your advert accounts today and switch off every setting that can alter creative after upload, then name one person who owns that panel.  A Japanese pizza chain published unapproved anime artwork last week because one of those settings had been left enabled, and viewers raised it before the brand did.
**3.** Count how many distinct things a viewer could want in your next seasonal film, and if the answer is one, add two more from ranges you already sell.  M&S put four ranges into one advert and posted 58 percent on the till question while the rest of the field sat between 32 and 42.
**4.** Demand peak, average concurrent and airtime together on every livestream sponsorship, and divide hours watched by airtime yourself when a seller has not given you the average.  IEM Beijing beat PGL Masters Bucharest on peak and delivered 38 percent less watch time, on a schedule nearly 20 hours shorter.
**5.** Write a co-streaming permission into your next live project before launch and name the creators you want using the feed.  The most-watched streamer on Twitch in October was one man narrating a tournament he does not own, at 22.2 million hours watched for the month, while no other creator passed 10 million hours.
**6.** Put the disclosure wording and placement you expect into the creator brief itself, and tell the creator in writing that nobody at your company may ask them to soften it.  Eighteen percent of creators surveyed say a brand asked them not to disclose a paid relationship in the last year, and the exposure reaches the advertiser.
**7.** Sort your footage into claim and mood before you commission anything generated, and permit generation only in the mood column.  Mark Rober's team keeps AI on scripts and thumbnails and away from the camera, because on a demonstration channel the unbroken shot is the receipt.
